titulo: Quiz — Γεια σας on the way in, and nine more words
subtitulo: The word that opens and closes, the one that does three jobs, and the hour nobody has fixed
introPt: A traveller walks into a small shop in the middle of the afternoon and leaves two minutes later.
cenario: A small shop just after two in the afternoon, the owner behind the counter.

perguntas.pergunta: Which greeting is safe with a shopkeeper you have never met?
opcoes: Γεια σου, every time
Γεια σας — it covers anyone you are not close to, and more than one person
Neither; you need a different word for shops
Whichever one is shorter
perguntas.explica: Use γεια σας always and you never have to decide. When γεια σου comes back at you, that is warmth arriving, not a correction.

perguntas.pergunta: How many jobs does παρακαλώ do?
opcoes: One — please
Three — please, you're welcome, and go ahead
Two — please and sorry
It is only used on the telephone
perguntas.explica: Same four syllables, beat at the end, three positions. You will hear it far more often than you say it.

perguntas.pergunta: It is half past two. Καλημέρα or καλησπέρα?
opcoes: Καλημέρα — the rule says noon
There is no fixed hour; hand back whichever one reaches you, and γεια σας is safe at any time
Καλησπέρα — the rule says one o'clock
Neither is used in the afternoon
perguntas.explica: No normative source sets the switch. Three usages coexist, καλό μεσημέρι sits in the gap, and native speakers hesitate in that band too.

perguntas.pergunta: A question about your job or your hotel arrives quickly and directly. What is that?
opcoes: A sign that something is being asked of you
A standard move in a politeness system built on involvement rather than distance
Rudeness, and you should end the conversation
A translation error
perguntas.explica: The research describes two politeness systems, not two kinds of people. The mismatch runs both ways and produces two symmetrical misreadings.

perguntas.pergunta: What does Greece's position in the English proficiency indices allow you to say?
opcoes: A precise share of the population speaks English
It places among the high-proficiency countries in commercial self-selection indices — a direction, not a headcount
Almost nobody speaks English
Speaking is its strongest sub-score
perguntas.explica: The samples are online and self-selected, as the publisher itself states. Speaking is the lowest of the four sub-scores, which is exactly where a short Greek sentence pays.
